en:
...Still, I can't believe you're going on with this.
{a}, was it?
You've got some real guts, you know that?
Well?{p}Don't you actually want to quit already?
I want to quit
I don't want to quit
I like that.{p}

Still, it's gotten pretty lonely in here.
There were six of us at the start, and now we're down to three.
And the last one who's supposed to tell a story still hasn't shown up.
Well, I guess that doesn't matter.
No point making a fuss about it now.{p}

Well then, let me introduce myself.
My name's Makoto Shindo.
I'm a third-year.
Good to meet you.{p}

You know our school's got a whole pile of sports clubs that are regulars at the national tournament, right?
Baseball and soccer.
Judo and kendo.
Tennis and table tennis.
Well, we've got plenty of talent here.
Which means the teams run deep.
Anyway, among all those sports clubs, there was one that set just as many brilliant records as the ones I just named.
Though it's gone completely to seed these days.
Can you guess which one?{p}

...It's the boxing club.
Boxing's great.
It's a man's sport.
It's the kind of sport a woman can't really understand, right?
People who don't get boxing say it's just a slugfest, just a brawl, but that's dead wrong.
You'd be hard pressed to find a more gentlemanly sport anywhere, don't you think?
Our school's boxing club was really something back in the day, too.
It showed up at the nationals pretty much every single year.
And it placed near the top in a whole bunch of weight classes.
Pretty impressive, isn't it?{p}

But now it's no good.
No good at all.
The membership's dropped way off, too.
There's not a trace left of what it used to be.
It's turned into a ghost club, clinging to its past glory and only still around out of pity.
But there's a bit of a story behind that.
The scary story I'm going to tell you is about that boxing club.{p}

The boxing club didn't just get strong on its own.
And it's not like only guys with talent sign up, either.
In sports, guts count for more than talent.
The boxing club got strong by beating those guts into shape.
That's what they call hazing.
It's not bullying, mind you.
It's hazing.{p}
Our boxing club had a traditional kind of hazing that got handed down from one generation to the next.{p}You know what kind of hazing it was?
A thousand bunny hops
Running to the shrine
Brutal alumni training
The Hell Camp

That's right, the one they also call the Hell Camp.
When summer vacation comes, they hole up in the mountains for three whole weeks.
Of course, there's brutal training before that, too.
Hazing from the alumni, three round trips running to the shrine.{p}

At the start, there are about forty new members.
The tough training cuts that down to about half.
And then comes the summer Hell Camp.
The twenty or so who somehow made it that far get whittled down to five at this camp.
Bet that surprised you, huh?
But those five are strong, let me tell you.
After all, they're the five who survived the Hell Camp.
Their guts are on a whole other level.
They're the ones who carry the boxing club's tradition and pass it on.{p}...So, do you want to know what goes on at that camp?
I want to know
I don't want to know

Hm hm... So you want to know, huh?
You're really into this stuff, aren't you?
You just love cruel stories, is that it?
Or are you the type who loves other people's misery?
Well, whatever.
Then I'll tell you.{p}

In the morning, they get up at four, chop firewood and do morning practice.
Then they make breakfast.
After they eat, it's weight training and running the mountain trails.
That's rough, let me tell you.{p}

Then they make lunch.
The first-years do all the cooking, see.
And if it tastes bad, they get punched out.
On top of that, three hundred push-ups.
Just because the food tasted bad.
That's torture, isn't it?
But that's just the beginning.
If that was all, it wouldn't be bad enough to be called the Hell Camp.{p}

The real trouble is the afternoon.
In the afternoon, the first-years, one at a time, spar against every single senior.
Three rounds with each one.
There are only about ten seniors, but they're guys who place near the top at the nationals.
You get made to fight those guys for thirty rounds total.
It's nothing but torture.
They call it hazing, but frankly, it's just bullying.{p}

Well, hardly anybody lasts to the end.
They usually end up passing out partway through.
Even when they pass out, they get water dumped on them and get hauled back to their feet.
And then they're made to keep fighting.
A living punching bag.
A leather sack stuffed with flesh and blood instead of sand.
In a single day, the first-years' faces swell up like balloons. It's a parade of monsters.{p}

And guys like that are crawling all over, deep in the mountains.
If some hiker happened to stumble across them...
Maybe that's what ghosts really are, huh?
Ah ha ha ha...
...Well, let's keep going.{p}

So anyway, they keep up that training, or torture, or bullying, whatever you want to call it, right?
Within three days, most of the guys have run off, just like that.
They sneak away in the middle of the night.
And in the end, they're down to about five.
Let's see, how many years ago was it?
I think it was about fifteen years ago.
That year, the Hell Camp was held just like every other year.
Twenty-three first-years took part in the camp.
They'd all heard the rumors about the camp, see.
Most of them were nervous wrecks, but a few of them were calm.
They were sure of themselves, saying they'd be fine.
Though it's always guys like that who end up being the first to run off.{p}
Now, among the first-years that year was a guy named Yosuke Akasaka.

You couldn't really call him the sturdy type.
But he loved boxing.
He idolized strong boxers.
He looked like the type who gets picked on, Akasaka did.
Honestly, the seniors figured he'd be the very first to quit.
But it turned out he had guts.
Say what you will, he lasted all the way to the camp.
Still, everyone was sure he'd have quit by the time the camp was over.
And with that in mind, they zeroed in on Akasaka as their target.
The target of their hazing.{p}

Frankly, call it hazing or training or whatever, but I think for the seniors it was also a way to blow off steam and work off stress.
On the surface, they said all the right things, about honoring tradition and building mental toughness that way.
But in reality, it was nothing of the sort.
It really was just bullying.{p}
And they decided to ask Akasaka to come along.{p}What do you think Akasaka said?
Let's run away together
I'll stick it out to the end
Say that and I'll tell the seniors on you

Akasaka had guts.
No matter how hard they tried to talk him into it, he wouldn't run.
He insisted he'd see the camp through to the end.
But here's the thing.
Once he said that, the first-years who'd suggested the escape suddenly got worried.
They'd been sure Akasaka would go along with it, see.
That's why they'd asked him.
But he flatly refused.
And that made them nervous.{p}

Akasaka was sure to report this to the seniors.
Then they'd be the ones on the receiving end of the hazing.
It was hard enough already. If they got any more, they'd really die.
They all started shaking like leaves.
Then they crowded in on Akasaka.
"Hey.
You keep this a secret, got it?"
"...Yeah, I won't tell."
But none of them believed what Akasaka said.
Even if they wanted to believe him, they were worried sick.{p}

So they called him out.
While they were making dinner, they ganged up on Akasaka and beat him.
Pretty awful, huh?
They all had a lot of pent-up frustration, see.
At first, they only meant to rough him up a little.
But it didn't stop there.
It kept escalating.
Maybe Akasaka was just the kind of guy who gets picked on by nature.
Like they were possessed by something, they all punched and kicked Akasaka.{p}

"I'm borrowing your gloves."
The ringleader was a guy named Toru Hatanaka.
He took Akasaka's gloves and pounded on Akasaka like he was a real punching bag.
"S-stop it... What did I ever do to you?"
"Heh.
You haven't done anything yet, so we're taking care of it now, while we can.
If we leave you alone, you'll rat on us for sure.
Listen, don't you dare rat to the seniors that we tried to run away."
And with that, he punched Akasaka over and over and over again.{p}

"Got it?!
Don't you dare rat on us!"
"............"
Akasaka didn't answer any more after that.
"Hey, Toru.
That's enough.
He's out cold."
If one of them hadn't stopped him, Hatanaka would have kept on beating Akasaka.{p}

The gloves were smeared with blood.
Boxing gloves are red to begin with, right?
When they get blood on them, see, those worn-out old gloves shine and gleam like they're brand new.
"Here, you can have them back."{p}
He flung the gloves down, smashing them into Akasaka's face as he lay there limp.{p}

Then they all went back to making dinner.
They left Akasaka there, all alone.
"Hey! Where's Akasaka?"
Even at mealtime, Akasaka didn't show up.
Then again, it was normal for some of the first-years to feel too sick to eat.
So they could easily fool the seniors when they asked.
"Akasaka said he wasn't feeling well, so he's lying down, sir!"
The seniors didn't press any further.
After they'd cleared away the meal, Hatanaka and the others hurried to the spot where they'd beaten Akasaka.{p}

Akasaka was still there.
Lying limp, just the way they'd left him.
"Hey, Akasaka!
Quit fooling around and get up."
Hatanaka gave Akasaka a light kick in the stomach.
But something was off.
It was like kicking a lump of soft rubber. He didn't react at all.
Not the way a living person would.{p}

"...Hey, Toru!
He's dead!"
The guy who'd tried to help Akasaka up couldn't help shouting.
"...You're kidding, right?"
Hatanaka didn't believe it.
He never imagined a guy who'd held up under all that hazing would die from a little roughing up.
But he was dead.
No matter how they called his name, no matter how they shook him, he didn't so much as twitch.
He wasn't breathing.
"...What do we do, Toru?
We're screwed."
The guys who'd beaten Akasaka along with him sounded like they were about to die themselves.
Well, of course they did.
They'd killed someone.
And they'd all ganged up on him to do it...{p}So, what do you think they did?
Decided to just bury the body
Reported it to the seniors
Carried him to a futon and laid him down

"L-let's bury him."
Hatanaka muttered it under his breath, with a ghastly look on his face.
Everyone looked at Hatanaka's face, worried.
But maybe there really was no other way.{p}

That night, after everyone was asleep, they buried Akasaka's body.
In secret.
Running away was the last thing on their minds now.
"Where'd Akasaka go?!"
Even when the seniors yelled, they all just put on innocent faces and cocked their heads.
"...He looked like he was having a hard time.
I bet he ran off."
And that satisfied everybody.
He'd been on the list of likely dropouts from the start, after all.
Some of the seniors even nodded like they were glad.
Pretty smug of them, huh?{p}

As for Hatanaka and the others, they spent the rest of the camp jumpy and scared that they'd be found out.
Maybe that actually helped, because Hatanaka and his bunch made it through the Hell Camp.
Turning misfortune into a blessing... is that how the saying goes?
That's exactly what happened.{p}

Once you make it through the camp, you're a full-fledged member.
First-years who'd been treated like bugs until then finally get recognized as human beings.
And they gain confidence, too.
So they get stronger fast.
Say what you want, that camp really does work.
But the Akasaka business did turn into a problem.
Even if he'd run away from camp, he never made it back home.{p}

A search party went out.
But they didn't find him.
Hatanaka and the others were scared out of their minds about what would happen if the body turned up.
Even so, nothing was found, and the search was called off.
After that, Hatanaka and the rest didn't have a care in the world.
They forgot all about Akasaka in no time.
...And then a year went by.{p}

Hatanaka and the others were second-years now.
This time, it was their turn to haze the first-years.
They went at it brutally, like they were paying back everything they'd been through.
Now that it was their turn, it really hit them how much fun hazing could be.
The club that had been so painful until then turned rosy overnight.
Then the annual summer camp drew near.
But along with it, the memory of Akasaka came back to them.{p}

Going to camp meant going to that place.
They'd have to go to the place where Akasaka was buried.
"What do we do, Toru?
Are you going to the camp?"
The guys who'd been in on it back then all looked uneasy.{p}
Well?{p}Do you think Hatanaka went to the camp?
He went
He didn't go

"I'm going.
What, you guys chickening out? Morons."
Hatanaka forced himself to act tough.
He was really scared, but he pretended it was nothing.
Once Hatanaka said that, the others had no choice but to join the camp too.
They were scared of what would be done to them if they didn't.
If anyone betrayed him, there was no telling what Hatanaka would do, and they all knew that better than anyone.{p}
And so the Hell Camp began.{p}

Hatanaka and his bunch hazed the first-years without mercy.
Even when somebody collapsed, they never let up.
And one after another, guys ran away.
Even so, the ones who made it through this camp would be the ones to build the club's next era. Thinking that way, they could fully justify what they were doing, and they felt no guilt at all.{p}

"Huh?
These gloves..."{p}

"Aaagh!"
Hatanaka yelled as he picked them up.
The moment he grabbed those gloves, he felt something slimy and lukewarm.
That's right, what he felt was blood.
"Th-these... these are Akasaka's!"
Hatanaka couldn't stop shaking.
And he ran from the spot.{p}

Later, once he'd calmed down, he thought it over.
Were those really Akasaka's gloves?
Or was it somebody's prank?
No, maybe he'd just seen wrong.{p}What do you think Hatanaka did?
Went back to check
Went to where they'd buried the body
Told the others

That night, Hatanaka told the others.
All the guys who'd taken part in that little game back then.
"Don't be stupid, Toru.
No way that happened."
"Weren't you just dreaming?"
They all laughed it off.
But their eyes weren't laughing.
Deep down, every one of them was trembling with fear.{p}

"...Did you guys bury Akasaka's gloves with him back then?"
As they all sat in silence, Hatanaka looked around at each of them and asked.
They looked at each other.
Now that he asked, they couldn't really remember.
After all, it had happened a year ago.
They'd buried the body, sure, but had they buried the gloves along with it?{p}

They'd been so caught up in burying the body... maybe they'd forgotten to bury the gloves?
No, that couldn't be.
If they'd forgotten them, the search party would have found those gloves.
Then... was it someone's prank?{p}

"Should we go check it out?"
Everyone was stunned by Hatanaka's words.
Why would they go back on their own to the one place they never wanted to see again?
"...Just kidding."
Hatanaka laughed, taking back what he'd said.
They all seemed relieved to hear that.
And that was the end of the day.
Every one of them fell asleep thinking about Akasaka.{p}

The next day.
After morning practice and lunch, Hatanaka and the others waited eagerly for the afternoon hazing.
They went to the makeshift ring and focused their minds on the hazing to come, trying to shake off all thoughts of Akasaka.
"...That's weird.
Nobody's coming.
What are the seniors and the first-years doing?"
Practice time came, and still nobody showed.
"Hey, here comes one!"
While they were wondering what was going on, a single figure came toward them with a towel draped over his head.
They couldn't tell who it was, but it didn't seem to be one of the seniors.
"You're late!
Get over here, now!"
Itching to get started, Hatanaka couldn't hold himself back and shouted roughly.{p}

The guy didn't answer.
He had bright red gloves on his hands, and he came slowly, so slowly, swaying as he walked, as if his feet weren't touching the ground.
"...Sorry to keep you waiting."
It was a weak little voice you could barely hear.
"Hurry up and get in the ring.
I'll whip you into shape myself."
With that, it was Hatanaka who climbed into the ring.
"...I'm in your hands."
The guy climbed into the ring, slow and stiff.
His body was like a skeleton's.
"Come on, get that towel off already!"{p}

Hatanaka snatched the towel off the guy's head and couldn't believe his eyes.
That's right... it was Akasaka, no doubt about it.
"...A-Akasaka."
That was all Hatanaka could manage to say.{p}

"...Now, put on these gloves and hit me, will you?"
With that, Akasaka pulled the gloves off his own hands.
They really were like a skeleton's hands.
Only the tendons of his fingers bulged out; it was as if skin alone were stuck to the bone.
"D-don't, Akasaka... I'm sorry, it was my fault."
Hatanaka couldn't move.
It was as if roots had sprouted from his feet; he couldn't take a single step.
And it wasn't just Hatanaka.
Not one of the guys there who had killed Akasaka could move.
"............"
Akasaka didn't answer.
Then he pulled off Hatanaka's gloves and put his own gloves on him instead.{p}

"Gyaaah!"
The moment the gloves were on him, Hatanaka's face twisted in agony and he screamed.{p}

Hatanaka weakly raised his fists and pounded on Akasaka with them.
It was more like stroking him than hitting him.
And yet, for some reason, Hatanaka, the one doing the hitting, was the one who looked like he was in pain.
Then red blood began to trickle out of the gaps in the gloves.
"F-forgive me, Akasaka.
It hurts! Please, stop it!"
"Being made to hit him" was exactly the right way to put it.
Akasaka told him to, and it was as if Hatanaka were being controlled.{p}

"...Now, it's your turn."
Once Hatanaka had finished his round of hitting, Akasaka's eyes came to rest on someone else.
That guy screamed and struggled, but his legs wouldn't obey him, and they carried him up into the ring on their own.
Akasaka slowly pulled the gloves off Hatanaka's hands.{p}

Hatanaka's hands were stained bright red with blood.
And out of the gloves came tumbling old, blood-soaked nails.
Akasaka's gloves had been crammed full of nails.
The moment they came off, Hatanaka collapsed on the spot, shuddered two or three times, and then lay still.
He'd passed out from the shock.{p}

"...Go on, it's your turn."
And he pulled the nail-filled gloves tight onto the hands of the guy who'd just climbed into the ring.{p}

Nobody could get away.
Every one of them was at Akasaka's mercy.
One by one, Akasaka carried out his bloody punishment.
Without sparing a single one.{p}

They were found behind the camp lodge.
...That's right, the place where they'd buried Akasaka.
Maybe they'd been seeing things.
And maybe Akasaka's ghost had lured them there.
When they were found, Hatanaka and the others were all dead.
With their hands soaked in blood.{p}

Every one of them died of shock, apparently.
They say a single pair of mud-caked gloves was lying nearby.
Unusually heavy gloves, stuffed with old nails.
After that incident, the boxing club went downhill in no time.
Nobody joined anymore, and everybody quit like they were running away.{p}

That's the end of my story.
...How do I know a story like this?
You think it's strange that I know all this, when there's no way I could've been there?
You think I made it up, right?
If you want to think that, go ahead.
Only a handful of people know the truth.
Well, you can take it as a funny joke if you like.
All right, who's talking next?
Hurry up and get on with it.{p}
...Hey, {a}.{p}Don't you want to know what Akasaka looked like?
I want to know
I don't want to know
So you want to know, huh?{p}

Heh... The newspaper club keeps the graduation album from every year, right?
Look for the album from thirteen years ago.
The photo of Class F from that year.
Akasaka's in it.{p}

After Shindo said that, I decided to look for it.
...If I remembered right, the graduation albums were kept on this shelf.
...This is the one.
I opened it to the group photo of Class F.{p}

In the corner of the group photo, set apart in a frame, was a picture of Akasaka.
...So this is what he looked like.
But next to it was one more person, also set in a frame.
...Toru Hatanaka.
I see... if Shindo's story was true, Hatanaka had died too, so of course he'd be in a frame too.{p}

Huh?
I took a closer look at Hatanaka's photo, and my eyes were nailed to it.{p}

...No way.
...No way, this face...
I was at a loss for words.
He looked just like Shindo.
No, "just like" didn't begin to cover it.
It was him, in the flesh.
"Shindo!"
I tore my eyes from the album and turned around.{p}

...He was gone.
Shindo was nowhere to be seen.
"Where's Shindo?"
I asked the two who were left.
They were both startled.
They'd both been looking at the album with me, so maybe they hadn't noticed Shindo leave.
Or... was he a ghost?{p}

"This Hatanaka guy looks just like Shindo, doesn't he?"
One of the two who were left said it in a shaking voice.{p}

"...Hey, what are we going to do?
I'm starting to get really scared.
Can't we just stop?"
One of the two who were left was a girl.
She peered anxiously into my face.
It was creepy, no question.
The people who told stories were disappearing, one by one.
Whatever the reason, they were disappearing.
If we kept going like this, what on earth would happen?
...I agonized over it.
Should I keep going, or should I stop now?{p}What should I do?
Keep going
Stop now

...I couldn't stop.
Not after coming this far, I couldn't.
Whatever ending might be waiting for us, there was no turning back now.
Maybe by then something already had its hold on me.
"...Let's keep going.
I feel like it would be wrong to stop here."
Neither of them objected.
I looked from one face to the other.
Now, who should I ask to tell the next story?{p}

You want to quit, but you can't... is that it?
Oh well. Can't be helped.{p}

That's right, a thousand bunny hops.
Now that is some brutal training.
Let me tell you how it works.
You make the first-years do bunny hops around the schoolyard.
Bunny hops are rough, right?
Some guys drop to their knees before they've even made it once around.
When that happens, the upperclassmen scream at them with faces like demons.{p}
"Hop to it! A thou-sand times!☆"{p}

...Just kidding.
...
My bad.
Back to the story.
The traditional hazing happens at the training camp.{p}

Well, they did do that kind of thing, too.
But there's hazing that's way worse.
It's the one they call the Hell Camp.
When summer vacation comes, they hole up in the mountains for three whole weeks.
Of course, there's brutal training before that, too.
Like the runs to the shrine you just mentioned, or the alumni's brutal training.{p}

Well, they did do that kind of thing, too.
But there's hazing that's way worse.
It's the one they call the Hell Camp.
When summer vacation comes, they hole up in the mountains for three whole weeks.
Of course, there's hazing before that, too.
Like the alumni's brutal training you just mentioned, or the runs to the shrine.{p}

Don't say that.
I'm telling it, like it or not.{p}

Turns out Akasaka was only human after all.
It seems even he'd had about enough of that hazing.
He listened to them in silence for a while, then lowered his eyes like he'd made up his mind, and finally agreed to their idea of running away together.
Well, of course he did.
The boxing club's hazing really was insane.
But that guy was something else.
He said that if they were going to run away anyway, they should get revenge on the seniors first.
Here was his plan.{p}

Mix sleeping pills and a paralytic drug into dinner, then tie those guys up once they couldn't move.
Then, as payback for everything, use them as punching bags, beat them to a pulp, and skip out just like that...{p}

Everyone stared at Akasaka in shock.
But his eyes didn't show the slightest doubt or hesitation.
It's always the ones who seem quiet day to day who are scary at times like this, right?
Of course, everyone was against Akasaka's plan.
Just running away made them feel guilty enough; nobody wanted any part in something that terrifying.
But Akasaka was different.
He stubbornly kept insisting on actually carrying out that crazy idea.
And finally, he said that if they wouldn't help, he'd tell the seniors all about their escape.
Then it would all be for nothing.
So everyone reluctantly went along with Akasaka's plan.{p}

In the end, they decided to mix the paralytic into that day's dinner.
Only into the seniors' plates, of course.
The seniors happily gulped down the soup laced with sleeping pills and paralytic.
And then the lynching plan was carried out.
First, Akasaka made sure the seniors were out cold, then punched them in the gut as hard as he could.
Maybe that was the signal...
Everyone punched and kicked the seniors, like they were working off all their pent-up frustration.
Even the guys who'd been scared at first started getting into it.
They kept beating the seniors until their faces were swollen blue and a mess of nosebleeds.
...And in the middle of all that, it happened.{p}

"H-he's... dead☆"
"Hey, you were really laying into this senior, weren't you?"

"Don't give me that!
You beat him to a pulp too, didn't you?"
They all started pinning the blame on each other.
But that wasn't going to get them anywhere.
So in the end, they all agreed to cover the whole thing up.
How, you ask?
They pretended to be victims too.
Faked it, basically.{p}

Just like the seniors, they made it look like somebody had drugged them and beaten them black and blue.
They all punched each other, lay down in the same place as the seniors, and waited for somebody to find them.{p}

That 'somebody' didn't show up until the next morning.
An alumnus who'd come to put his beloved juniors through the wringer found them all lying in the dining hall.
"What the hell happened here★"
Can't blame the guy for being shocked.
The toughest fighters of a boxing club ranked among the best in the country were sprawled on the floor in a pitiful state.
"Call the police!"
"No, an ambulance!"
I hear it was total chaos.
In the end, a paralyzing drug was found on the dishes left at the scene, and it was ruled the work of someone with a grudge against the boxing club.{p}

A club member who couldn't take the seniors' hazing and ran away...
A rival school's boxing club that always lost to them in matches...
Back then, there were mountains of people with a grudge against the boxing club.
It all went exactly the way Akasaka had scripted it.{p}

What's wrong, {a}?
Why the scary face...
Does it bug you that much that Akasaka and the others got away with their cover-up?
You think they should've been punished, right?
Man, you're an impatient one.
Well, just hear my story out to the end.{p}

Their injuries were pretty light compared to the seniors'.
It was all faked, after all.
On top of that, the second- and third-years who were the club's core were too hurt to move, right?
So ironically, it fell to Akasaka and the other first-years to carry the boxing club.{p}

And get this: Akasaka, of all people, was racking up some pretty impressive results.
Maybe something changed inside him after that incident, huh?
Like he'd found out how good it felt to hit people... you know.
He'd always had guts, so I think he had the talent for it.{p}

...And then a year went by.
They were second-years now.
This time it was their turn to haze the first-years.
The first-years that year had real rotten luck.{p}

Nobody said it out loud, but everyone involved in the incident a year earlier couldn't hide how uneasy they were.
Akasaka was no different.
If he'd had his way, maybe he wouldn't have gone to the summer camp at all.
But that wasn't an option, right?
